subject.title: fix #95279: Provide a trusted inbound-decoration contract so consumers can strip/dedup without forgeable text heuristics

question: Should OpenClaw accept this trusted inbound-decoration contract as top-level `inboundDecorated`/`bareBody` fields, or require the same data to live under an OpenClaw-owned metadata envelope before merge?
rationale: The fix changes durable session-message state and exported `MsgContext` shape across plugins and transcript consumers; code review can verify the branch behavior, but maintainers must choose the permanent compatibility boundary.

options.title: Accept Current Top-Level Fields
options.body: Merge the current additive shape after normal exact-head validation, treating `inboundDecorated` and `bareBody` as the approved durable contract for marked inbound turns.

options.title: Move Under OpenClaw Metadata
options.body: Ask the branch to store the trusted decoration data under an OpenClaw-owned metadata slot before merge to keep generic message fields narrower.

options.title: Pause Contract Work
options.body: Keep the PR and linked issue open until maintainers settle a broader message-state contract direction.

recommendation.title: Accept Current Top-Level Fields
recommendation.body: Merge the current additive shape after normal exact-head validation, treating `inboundDecorated` and `bareBody` as the approved durable contract for marked inbound turns.

likelyOwner.reason: Most directly tied to the current sentinel-strip UI/history behavior and later inbound-meta hardening history.
